title: Validation rules and error-message design
objectives: Define a validation rule as a formula that is true when the record is invalid and must not save.
Write an error message that tells the user what to fix, and choose top-of-page versus field location.
Use validation for cross-field and conditional requiredness that layouts and field Required cannot express.
Refuse validation when the need is a calculated display, a roll-up, a page-layout hide, or a long-running process.
diagnostic_question: Commercial properties must have a region, city must match region, and inspectors want a friendly message on the city field. Which parts are a validation rule, which are a dependent picklist, and where do you put the error message?
definition: A validation rule is a formula evaluated on save. When the formula is true, Salesforce blocks the save and shows an error message you write. Formula fields, rules, and other formula contexts share operators and functions, with some functions limited by context—VLOOKUP is available in validation rules, not as a general formula-field child lookup. Validation formulas may span related records through lookup or master-detail. ([Formula Operators and Functions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.usefulFormulaFields.meta/usefulFormulaFields/customize_functions.htm); [VLOOKUP](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_vlookup.htm); [Formula Field Limits and Restrictions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.formula_field_limits.htm); [Tips for Building Cross-Object Formulas](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm))
why_it_matters: The interview trap is inverting the formula (true means valid) or using a formula field as a gate. Another trap is a cryptic error message. Layout required and field Required cannot express 'required if Commercial.' Dependent picklists prevent bad combinations; validation is the backstop for conditions they cannot express, including API loads.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an airport security gate. The validation formula is the alarm: it is true when the suitcase must not pass. The error message is the sign the traveler can actually act on—'Put Region on Commercial properties' beats 'Invalid data.' You can hang the sign on the whole counter (top of page) or on one bin (a field). A reprint screen (formula field) does not lock the gate. A furniture arrangement (page layout) does not stop a cargo API.
deeper_explanation: Validation rules use the same formula language as formula fields, with context differences. The rule formula describes the error condition (true = invalid). That polarity is the opposite of how learners first guess. ([Formula Operators and Functions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.usefulFormulaFields.meta/usefulFormulaFields/customize_functions.htm))

VLOOKUP looks up a value on a custom object and is only available in validation rules. Constraints include matching the Record Name field on a custom object and returning certain field types. ([VLOOKUP](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.customize_functions_vlookup.htm))

Formula Field Limits: formula fields and formulas for approvals or rules can reference related records through lookup or master-detail. Record-type default-value formulas cannot span the same way. Campaign statistic fields cannot be referenced in validation rules (but can in custom formula fields). ([Formula Field Limits and Restrictions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.formula_field_limits.htm))

Error-message design is handbook quality on top of the official message field: say what is wrong and what to do, in the user's language, without internal API names. Location: field versus top of page. Exact character limits are Needs verification in current Help—do not invent them.

Validation is not a formula field, not a roll-up, not Dynamic Forms visibility, not a Flow that should run after a successful save, and not FLS. It does fire for many API and UI saves—confirm bypasses (such as some user permissions) in current Help before promising it always fires.

mental_model.analogy: An airport security gate: the formula is the alarm that is true when the bag must not pass, and the error message is the sign the traveler can act on.
useful_mapping: field location → sign taped to one bin
top of page → sign on the whole counter
layout required → a polite furniture note the cargo API can walk around
formula field → a reprint screen that does not lock the gate
dependent picklist → the bin that never offers the wrong city
where_it_breaks: Some permissions or tools may bypass validation—Needs verification; do not promise universal enforcement.
VLOOKUP rules are specific; the gate analogy does not encode Record Name matching.
Order of execution with Flow and Apex is a later topic; this lesson is the rule itself.
Character limits for messages are not quoted here.

claims.claim: Validation rules use the shared formula language. The formula is written so that a true result is the error condition that blocks the save.
claims.validation: Formula functions guide plus rules-as-formula-context in limits.

claims.claim: VLOOKUP is only available in validation rules. It matches lookup_value to the Record Name field on a custom object and returns a typed field; the first match wins.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A validation rule formula is true when the record is invalid. Salesforce blocks the save and shows your error message on a field or the page. Use it for conditional requiredness and API backstop. Do not invert the formula. Do not use a formula field as a gate.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I write AND/OR so true means stop. Commercial AND ISBLANK(Region) is the rule. The message says to enter Region for Commercial properties and sits on Region. I use dependent picklists for city/region combos when I can. I mention VLOOKUP only in validation. I mention spanning and the 10-relationship cap. I do not quote unofficial bypass lists.

when_to_use: When a save must fail because a formula condition is true (invalid record).
When requiredness depends on record type, picklist, or a parent field—not a simple field Required.
When you need an actionable error message on a field or at the top of the page.
When a dependent picklist is not enough and API users could still send a bad combination.
When VLOOKUP against a custom object's Record Name is the documented validation-only lookup.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a validation rule to calculate a display value (formula field) or to aggregate children (roll-up).
Do not use a validation rule as the first tool when a dependent picklist or record type already prevents the value.
Do not use a validation rule to hide fields (page layout or Dynamic Forms) or as FLS.
Do not invert the formula so true means valid.
Do not write 'Invalid data' as the only error message.

interview_questions.question: How does a validation rule work, and how do you write the formula?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The formula is the error condition. When it is true, Salesforce blocks the save and shows your error message. Write the bad case, not the good case.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I say true means invalid. I contrast formula fields, layout required, and dependent picklists. I mention spanning and the unique-relationship cap. I mention VLOOKUP as validation-only. I do not invent bypasses or message length limits.
follow_ups: Where do you put the message?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying the formula must return false to error

interview_questions.question: Commercial properties must have Region in UI and Data Loader.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A validation rule true when Commercial and Region are blank, with an actionable message on Region. Layout required on one layout is not enough.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still subset picklists and layouts. I test a Residential row so polarity is right. I run a LAB_ Data Loader update. If it succeeds, I did not actually have a rule. I do not use a formula checkbox as the gate.
interview_questions.example: Commercial blank Region fails UI and loader; Residential blank Region saves.

interview_questions.question: Write a better error message than Invalid data.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Say the business condition and the fix: Enter a Region for Commercial properties. Put it on the Region field when that is the fix.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I avoid API names unless admins are the only audience. I use the object's words (property, region, commercial). I use top of page if two fields conflict. I mark character limits Needs verification instead of guessing.
interview_questions.example: Message on Region__c, not a stack trace.
follow_ups: What if the field is not on the layout?

interview_questions.question: When is VLOOKUP the answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a validation rule must compare a value to a custom object's Record Name and return another typed field. It is not a formula-field function and not a child COUNT.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I recite Help constraints: custom object, Record Name match, allowed return types, first match wins. I prefer a real relationship or a dependent picklist if the model can hold the link. I do not put VLOOKUP on a formula field.
interview_questions.example: Block LAB_Zip__c values not found as LAB_AllowedZip__c.Name.
follow_ups: What if the custom object is deleted?
weak_answer_warnings: Using VLOOKUP in a formula field

interview_questions.question: City must match region. Is validation the first tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. Build a dependent picklist so users cannot pick the illegal city. Add validation only if APIs or integrations can still send the combo.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep DATA-008 in front. Validation is a gate, not a picker. If I add a rule, the message says which cities are valid for that region or tells them to pick city again after region. I do not replace the matrix with a giant OR formula if the picklist can do it.
interview_questions.example: Region→City matrix plus an optional API backstop rule.
follow_ups: How do you test the API path?
Does the rule consume a unique relationship?
weak_answer_warnings: Validation-only city control in the UI

interview_questions.question: Every save fails after you activate a rule.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The formula is probably true for valid rows. Invert or tighten the condition. Test a known-good LAB_ record.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look for a missing NOT, a blank compare that is always true, or a spanning field that is blank on every row. I deactivate in sandbox, fix, retest good and bad. I do not delete the object. I do not add another rule on top.
interview_questions.example: Rule was NOT(ISBLANK(Name)) which is true whenever Name is filled.
follow_ups: How do you debug the formula result?
Could record type be null on create?
weak_answer_warnings: Turning off all validation in the org

interview_questions.question: Validation rule versus before-save Flow versus formula field?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Formula field displays. Validation blocks a bad save. Before-save Flow can fix or enrich data when blocking is the wrong product. AUTO-001 owns the deeper tool choice.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use validation when the business wants a hard stop and a message. I use Flow when we should default Region rather than error. I do not hide fields with validation. I mention order of execution only at a high level and mark details neighboring.
interview_questions.example: Block blank Region on Commercial; Flow defaults Status to New instead of erroring.
follow_ups: Who sees the Flow fault path?
Does Flow run if validation fails?
weak_answer_warnings: Using Flow for every required field

interview_questions.question: How do validation rules share limits with formula fields?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: They share the formula language and the 10 unique-relationship cap across formula fields, rules, and lookup filters. Some functions and merge fields are context-specific, such as VLOOKUP and campaign statistic fields.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I audit existing walks before a spanning rule. I do not quote compile size without current Help. I mention record-type default formulas are narrower than rules. I keep roll-ups out of the story except as the wrong tool for aggregates.
interview_questions.example: A new spanning validation on Opportunity is rejected until an unused unique relationship is freed.
tradeoffs: Reuse a walk vs new parent
follow_ups: Do approval rules count in the same cap?
What is the current compile size?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying validation has no relationship budget
